literal: ] yet it was not implemented.
idiomatic: Yet the measure was never carried out.

literal: After Emperor Taizu of Song performed the eastern plowing, he then promulgated it to the commanderies, prefectures, and counties, all fully preparing the rite.
idiomatic: After Song Taizu performed the eastern plowing ceremony, the rite was promulgated to every commandery, prefecture, and county, each fully observing it.

literal: The Rites of Zhou: the queen leads inner and outer appointed wives to raise silkworms at the northern suburb.
idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou prescribe that the queen lead the palace ladies and appointed wives to raise silkworms at the northern suburb.

literal: The Han used the eastern suburb; this is not ancient.
idiomatic: The Han used the eastern suburb—a departure from antiquity.

literal: Wei used the northern suburb, following the Rites of Zhou.
idiomatic: Wei restored the northern suburb, in accord with the Rites of Zhou.

literal: Jin used the western suburb; presumably this paired with the plowing-field rite in the opposing direction.
idiomatic: Jin chose the western suburb, likely to mirror the sacred plowing field across the compass.

literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Huangchu, Emperor Wen of Wei ordered the inner palace to raise silkworms at the northern suburb.
idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year of Huangchu, Emperor Wen of Wei ordered the inner palace to raise silkworms at the northern suburb.

literal: According to Wei Dan\'s Ode on the Queen\'s Silkworm Rite, at that time the Han commentaries were already lost, and the ceremony was newly investigated and composed.
idiomatic: Wei Dan\'s ode on the queen\'s silkworm rite shows that by then the Han commentaries were lost and the ceremony had to be reconstructed from scratch.

literal: When it came to the Jin dynasty, the Prior Silkworm rite largely followed Wei practices.
idiomatic: Under the Jin, the Prior Silkworm rite largely followed Wei precedent.

literal: In the sixth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, Attendant Cavalier Hua Qiao memorialized: "The institutions of the former kings: the Son of Heaven and feudal lords personally plow the thousand mu; the queen and principal wife personally raise silkworms at the mulberry palace.
idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taikang, Attendant Cavalier Hua Qiao submitted a memorial: "By the ordinance of the ancient kings, the Son of Heaven and feudal lords personally plow the sacred thousand mu, and the queen and principal consort personally tend silkworms at the palace mulberry grove.

literal: Now Your Majesty, with sage brilliance and utmost benevolence, carries on the line of the former kings; the empress embodies the virtue of nurturing life and harmonizes with the meaning of pairing with Heaven—yet instruction has not been placed first, and the silkworm rite remains incomplete.
idiomatic: Your Majesty, in sage brilliance and deepest benevolence, continues the work of the ancient kings; the empress embodies the nurturing virtue of Heaven\'s creative power—yet moral instruction has not been set first, and the silkworm rite remains neglected.

literal: He considered it appropriate to follow the ancient form and complete this grand ceremony.
idiomatic: It would be fitting to follow the ancient pattern and restore this grand ceremony.

literal: " The edict said: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven personally plowed the sacred field to supply sacrificial grain; the queen and principal wife personally raised silkworms to provide sacrificial garments.
idiomatic: The emperor replied: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven personally plowed the sacred field to supply sacrificial grain, and the queen and principal consort personally raised silkworms to provide vestments for the altars.

literal: This was to earnestly observe filial reverence and clearly teach by example.
idiomatic: This was how filial reverence was earnestly upheld and moral instruction plainly shown.

literal: Now the plowing-field rite has its regulations, but the silkworm rite is not maintained.
idiomatic: Today the plowing-field rite is regulated, yet the silkworm ceremony goes unobserved.

literal: In the interim affairs were many, and there was no leisure to honor and complete it.
idiomatic: Pressing affairs in the intervening years left no time to restore it fully.

literal: Now the realm is at peace; the rites should be restored to show all within the four seas.
idiomatic: Now that the realm is at peace, the rite should be restored as an example to all under Heaven.

literal: Its details should follow classical texts and recent precedents, consulting what suits the present.
idiomatic: Draw the details from classical sources and recent precedent, adapting them to present needs.

literal: It shall be implemented next year.
idiomatic: It shall be carried out next year.

literal: " Thereupon Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Can was ordered to draft and fix the ceremony.
idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Can was charged with drafting the ceremonial regulations.

literal: The empress\'s mulberry-picking altar was west of the silkworm chamber, with a curtained pavilion outside the inner palace gate; the mulberry grove was east of it; the Prior Silkworm altar was outside the outer palace gate to the southeast.
idiomatic: The empress\'s mulberry-picking altar stood west of the silkworm chamber, with a curtained pavilion outside the inner gate; the mulberry grove lay to the east, and the Prior Silkworm altar southeast of the outer gate.

literal: Six wives of commoners were chosen as Silkworm Mothers.
idiomatic: Six commoner wives were appointed Silkworm Mothers.

literal: When the silkworms were about to hatch, on an auspicious day the empress wore twelve hairpins, following Han and Wei precedent, dressed in green robes, riding a lacquered-canopy mica-panel secure carriage drawn by six horses.
idiomatic: When the silkworms were about to hatch, on an auspicious day the empress wore twelve hairpins, and following Han and Wei custom donned green robes and rode a lacquered-canopy carriage with mica inlay, drawn by six horses.

literal: The Lady Director wore the diao and chan insignia, bore the seal, accompanied her in the carriage, and carried mulberry baskets and hooks.
idiomatic: The Lady Director, wearing her diao and chan insignia and bearing the seal, rode alongside her carrying mulberry baskets and picking hooks.

literal: Princesses, the Three Ladies, Nine Concubines, hereditary wives, various grand imperial consorts, grand ladies of dukes, ducal ladies, county and township noblewomen, distinguished ladies of commanderies, marquises, dukes, and specially advanced ranks, outer hereditary wives, and appointed wives—all wore step-shaking headdresses and green robes, each carrying baskets and hooks in attendance.
idiomatic: Princesses, the Three Ladies, the Nine Concubines, hereditary consorts, imperial grand consorts, ducal grand ladies, ducal ladies, county and township noblewomen, wives of distinguished lords, external consorts, and appointed wives all wore swaying step headdresses and green robes, each carrying baskets and hooks in procession.

literal: On the day before the silkworm-raising, silkworms newly hatched in the silkworm palace were placed on trays.
idiomatic: On the eve of the ceremony, newly hatched silkworms from the silkworm palace were laid out on trays.

literal: On the day of personally tending mulberry, the Grand Invoker offered a full ta lao sacrifice to the Prior Silkworm.
idiomatic: On the day of the empress\'s mulberry picking, the Grand Invoker sacrificed a full ta lao to the Prior Silkworm.

literal: The empress arrived at the western suburb, ascended the altar; princesses and those below lined the east of the altar in attendance.
idiomatic: The empress came to the western suburb and ascended the altar; princesses and those of lower rank stood in attendance on the east side.

literal: The empress faced east, personally tended mulberry, and picked three branches;
idiomatic: Facing east, the empress personally picked three mulberry branches;

literal: imperial consorts and princesses each picked five branches;
idiomatic: imperial consorts and princesses each picked five;

literal: county and township noblewomen and those below each picked nine branches.
idiomatic: county and township noblewomen and those below each picked nine.

literal: All mulberry was handed to the Silkworm Mothers.
idiomatic: All the mulberry was given to the Silkworm Mothers.

literal: They returned to the silkworm chamber.
idiomatic: They then returned to the silkworm chamber.

literal: When the rite was finished, the empress returned to her informal seat; princesses and those below took their places in order; a feast was set and silk gifts distributed according to rank.
idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the empress returned to her seat; princesses and those below took their places in order, and a feast was held with silk gifts graded by rank.

literal: In the fourth year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, this rite was again restored.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu of Song restored the ceremony once more.

literal: In the twenty-second year of Jian\'an of Emperor Xian of Han, Wei built a Pan Palace south of Ye city.
idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Jian\'an, Wei built a Pan Palace south of Ye.

literal: In the fifth year of Huangchu of Emperor Wen of Wei, the Imperial Academy was established at Luoyang.
idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huangchu, Emperor Wen of Wei founded the Imperial Academy at Luoyang.

literal: During the Zhengshi era of the Qi King, Liu Fu submitted a memorial: "Since Huangchu, the Imperial Academy has been esteemed and established; for more than twenty years, those who have graduated are few indeed.
idiomatic: During the Zhengshi reign, Liu Fu submitted a memorial: "Since Huangchu the Imperial Academy has been honored and maintained, yet for more than twenty years scarcely anyone has completed its course.

literal: Because the selection of Erudites was treated lightly, students avoided corvée labor, sons of eminent families were ashamed to be of that company—hence there were no learners.
idiomatic: Erudites were chosen too casually; students enrolled to evade labor service; sons of great houses were ashamed to keep such company—so almost no one truly studied.

literal: Though it had the name, it lacked the substance; though teaching was set up, it achieved no result.
idiomatic: It bore the name without the substance; teaching was established without effect.

literal: Erudites should be chosen with high standards, selecting those whose conduct is a model for others and whose mastery of the classics qualifies them as teachers, to oversee instruction of the heir apparent\'s sons.
idiomatic: Choose Erudites of the highest caliber—men whose conduct sets the standard and whose command of the classics qualifies them to teach—and put them in charge of instructing the crown prince\'s sons.

literal: Following ancient law, sons and grandsons of officials of two thousand shi rank and above, from age fifteen upward, should all enter the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: Follow the ancient law: all sons and grandsons of officials ranked two thousand shi and above, from age fifteen, should enter the Imperial Academy.

literal: Let promotion and demotion be clearly regulated, setting forth paths of honor and disgrace.
idiomatic: Make promotion and demotion explicit, marking clear paths of honor and shame.

literal: " The proposal was not accepted.
idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

literal: In the eighth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, the relevant offices memorialized: "Imperial Academy students number more than seven thousand; those whose talent qualifies them for fourth rank may be retained.
idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taishi, officials reported: "The Imperial Academy holds more than seven thousand students; those whose talents fit fourth-rank appointment may remain.

literal: " The edict: "Those who have passed examination in the classics shall remain; the rest shall be sent back to their commanderies and kingdoms.
idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Those who have passed the classics examination may stay; the rest shall be sent home to their commanderies and kingdoms.

literal: Sons and grandsons of great ministers who are fit to receive instruction shall be ordered to enter the academy.
idiomatic: Sons of great ministers fit for instruction shall be enrolled.

literal: " In the second year of Xianning, the National University was established—referring to the noble scions of the state called "sons of the realm" in the Rites of Zhou, who received instruction from the Teacher.
idiomatic: In the second year of Xianning the National University was founded—the school for noble scions called "sons of the realm" in the Rites of Zhou, who were taught by the royal tutor.

literal: In the fifth year of Taikang, the Bright Hall, the Moat-enclosed Academy, and the Spirit Terrace were built and restored.
idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taikang the Bright Hall, the Royal Academy, and the Spirit Terrace were constructed.

literal: In the first year of Yong\'an of Sun Xiu, an edict said: "In antiquity when establishing a state, teaching came first.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yong\'an, Sun Xiu issued an edict: "In founding a state, education comes first.

literal: This was to guide the age and govern character, cultivating talent for the times.
idiomatic: This guides the age, shapes character, and nurtures talent for the times.

literal: Since Jianxing, affairs have been many and troubled; officials and people have largely pursued immediate concerns, abandoning the root for the branch, not following the ancient way.
idiomatic: Since Jianxing affairs have been turbulent; officials and commoners alike chase immediate gain, abandoning fundamentals for frills and straying from the ancient path.

literal: When what is honored is not pure, culture is harmed and custom corrupted.
idiomatic: When what is valued lacks purity, culture suffers and custom collapses.

literal: Let school officials be established according to old practice, Five Classics Erudites appointed, candidates examined and selected, and their stipends and honors increased.
idiomatic: Restore school officials as before, appoint Erudites for the Five Classics, examine and select candidates rigorously, and increase their stipends and honors.

literal: Among presently serving officials and sons of military officers who show aspiration and aptitude, let each take up study.
idiomatic: Among serving officials and sons of officers who show aptitude and desire to learn, let each pursue his studies.

literal: Each year conduct examinations, grade ranks, and grant office and rewards.
idiomatic: Hold yearly examinations, grade students by rank, and grant office and rewards accordingly.

literal: Let those who see it rejoice in its glory; let those who hear of it envy its renown.
idiomatic: Let those who witness it delight in its honors, and those who hear of it envy its fame.

literal: Thus purify royal transformation and elevate custom.
idiomatic: Thus royal culture may be purified and custom elevated.

literal: " Thereupon schools were established.
idiomatic: Schools were then established.

literal: When Emperor Yuan was Prince of Jin, at the beginning of Jianwu, Rapid Cavalry General Wang Dao submitted a memorial:
idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan was still Prince of Jin, at the opening of the Jianwu era, Rapid Cavalry General Wang Dao submitted a memorial:

literal: The root of governing and transforming lies in rectifying human relations.
idiomatic: The foundation of good government lies in setting human relations right.

literal: The rectification of human relations depends on establishing schools.
idiomatic: Right human relations depend on establishing schools.

literal: When schools are established and the Five Teachings made clear, moral transformation penetrates thoroughly, the constant relations are put in order, and people have shame and are reformed.
idiomatic: Once schools are in place and the Five Teachings clear, moral influence spreads, the constant relations fall into order, and people feel shame and reform themselves.

literal: The order of father and son, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, elder and younger is made smooth, and the righteousness between ruler and minister is secured.
idiomatic: The order of father and son, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, and elder and younger is restored, and the bond between ruler and minister is strengthened.

literal: This is what the Book of Changes calls "when the family is rectified, the realm is settled."
idiomatic: This is what the Book of Changes means by "when the family is set right, the realm is settled."

literal: Therefore the sage king covered them to nurture rectitude, teaching them from youth, so that transformation soaked into bone and flesh, habit became nature, as if spontaneous—daily moving toward goodness and away from wrong without knowing it.
idiomatic: The sage king therefore nourished rectitude from infancy, teaching the young until moral transformation soaked into their bones, habit became nature, and day by day they drifted toward goodness and away from wrong without even knowing it.

literal: When conduct was formed and virtue established, then they were fitted with rank.
idiomatic: Only after conduct was formed and virtue established were they fitted to office.

literal: Even the king\'s own son was ranked alongside the sons of the realm, made to know the Way before attaining eminence.
idiomatic: Even the king\'s own son was ranked alongside the other princes\' sons, taught the Way before granted eminence.

literal: In selecting talent and employing officers, all first rooted themselves in learning.
idiomatic: In choosing talent and appointing officers, all first looked to what had been learned in school.

literal: Thus the Rites of Zhou: the district grandee "presents the book of the worthy and able to the king, and the king bows and receives it."
idiomatic: Hence the Rites of Zhou: the district grandee "presents the roster of the worthy and able to the king, and the king bows and receives it."

literal: This was to honor the Way and esteem scholars.
idiomatic: This is how the Way was honored and scholars valued.

literal: When people know why scholars are valued, it is because the Way endures.
idiomatic: When people understand why scholars are honored, it is because the Way still lives among them.

literal: Then they withdraw to cultivate themselves; cultivating themselves they extend to their families; rectifying their families they extend to their districts; learning in the district they ascend to court.
idiomatic: They withdraw to cultivate themselves; from self-cultivation they extend to family; from a well-ordered family to a well-ordered district; and from district learning they rise to serve at court.

literal: Returning to the root and restoring the beginning, each seeking within himself—the earnest pursuit of simplicity flourishes, the way of superficial falsity fades; teaching makes it so.
idiomatic: Returning to fundamentals, each searching within himself—the earnest pursuit of simplicity flourishes and shallow pretense withers. Such is the power of education.

literal: Therefore in serving the ruler they are loyal; in governing those below they are benevolent—precisely what Mencius called "never benevolent yet abandoning one\'s parents, never righteous yet putting the ruler last."
idiomatic: Such men serve their ruler with loyalty and govern subordinates with benevolence—precisely what Mencius meant by "there has never been a man who was benevolent yet disowned his parents, or righteous yet put his ruler last."

literal: Recently the imperial net has lost coherence, ritual teaching has declined, eulogies are not raised—now for two twelve-year cycles.
idiomatic: In recent years the imperial order has lost coherence, ritual teaching has fallen into ruin, and the hymns of praise have fallen silent—for two full twelve-year cycles now.

literal: The tradition says: "If for three years ritual is not performed, ritual must collapse;
idiomatic: The tradition says, "If ritual goes unperformed for three years, it must collapse;

literal: if for three years music is not performed, music must fall to ruin."
idiomatic: if music goes unperformed for three years, it must fall to ruin."

literal: How much more when it has lasted so long?
idiomatic: And how much worse when the neglect has lasted this long?

literal: The elder generation gradually forgets the bearing of bowing and yielding; the young hear only the clash of arms and armor; war daily approaches, sacrificial vessels are not set forth; the way of the former kings grows ever distant; the wind of ornament and falsity thus spreads—this is not what is meant by accustoming the people and settling custom, rectifying the root and restraining the branch.
idiomatic: The older generation forgets the grace of bowing and yielding; the young hear only the clash of arms. War draws nearer day by day while sacrificial vessels gather dust. The way of the ancient kings recedes ever further, and the taste for ornament and pretense spreads—hardly the way to train the people, settle custom, strengthen fundamentals, and curb excess.

literal: Your Highness, with the endowment of one destined to reshape the age, stands at a moment of peril; in ritual, music, campaigning, and punitive expeditions you aid the revival—about to wash away filth and scour away blemish, set chaos aright and restore order.
idiomatic: Your Highness bears the talent of one born to reshape an age, entrusted with restoration at a moment of peril. Through ritual, music, and arms alike you have aided the revival, cleansing corruption and setting chaos aright.

literal: Truly you ought to plan and govern by examining antiquity, establish and clarify schools, unfold the Six Arts to instruct the young, so that the Way of wen and wu, fallen, may rise again.
idiomatic: You should truly take counsel from antiquity, establish schools, unfold the Six Arts to instruct the young, and revive the fallen Way of civil and martial excellence.

literal: At present the Minor Odes are wholly abandoned; barbarian enemies blaze and burn; integrity and righteousness decline; national humiliation is not yet washed away.
idiomatic: Today the Minor Odes lie abandoned; barbarian raiders burn across the land; integrity and righteousness falter; national humiliation remains unavenged.

literal: Loyal ministers and righteous men therefore clench their wrists and beat their breasts—ritual, music, governance, and punishment ought to be set forth together to aid one another.
idiomatic: Loyal ministers and righteous men clench their fists and burn with grief. Ritual, music, governance, and punishment must be deployed together if any is to succeed.

literal: If ritual and righteousness are firmly fixed and pure influence broadly harmonious, then what transformation molds is wide, what virtue covers is great, what righteousness attaches to is deep, and what awe strikes is far.
idiomatic: If ritual and righteousness are firmly rooted and pure influence spreads far, then transformation will reach widely, virtue will cover greatly, righteousness will run deep, and authority will be felt even at a distance.

literal: Proceeding from this, one could cross the river in court robes and cap, restore what was missing from the imperial canon, tighten what had slackened in the royal net; the glutton would change his heart, the beast\'s face would be transformed; by bowing and yielding the barbarians would submit; with loosened sash the realm would follow—once the Way is grasped, would it be difficult?
idiomatic: From there one might cross the Yellow River in court robes and restore what the imperial canon had lost, tighten the slackened royal net, turn savage hearts toward civilization, win the submission of barbarians through courtesy rather than force, and bind the realm with a loosened sash. Once the Way is truly grasped, would any of this be difficult?

literal: Thus Yu danced with shield and axe and the Three Miao were transformed; Duke Xi of Lu built the Pan Palace and the Huai Yi were pacified; the hegemony of Huan and Wen—all first taught, then fought.
idiomatic: Yu danced with shield and axe and the Three Miao submitted; Duke Xi of Lu built the Pan Palace and the Huai barbarians were pacified; the hegemonies of Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi all rested on teaching before fighting.

literal: Now if we earnestly follow former canons, revive the way of teaching, cause sons of the court to enter school together, and require all who seek to establish virtue and rise to office to master it before advancing—
idiomatic: If we now earnestly follow the ancient canon, restore the path of education, enroll the sons of the court in schools, and require all who seek office through virtue to master their studies before advancing—

literal: when the path of virtue opens and the road of falsity is blocked, then its transformation succeeds without severity, governance without harshness.
idiomatic: then the path of virtue will open, the road of pretense will close, and transformation will succeed without severity while order is kept without harshness.

literal: Choose clear-sighted, broad-learning, ritual-observant men as teachers; honor teaching and esteem the Way—transforming culture and fixing custom: nothing surpasses this.
idiomatic: Choose as teachers men of broad learning and ritual mastery; honor education and esteem the Way. Nothing surpasses this for transforming culture and fixing custom.

literal: Attendant Cavalier Dai Miao also submitted a memorial, saying:
idiomatic: Attendant Cavalier Dai Miao also submitted a memorial:

literal: I have heard that in what Heaven\'s Way operates, nothing is greater than yin and yang;
idiomatic: I have heard that in the operation of Heaven\'s Way, nothing is greater than yin and yang;

literal: the utmost task of emperors and kings, nothing is weightier than ritual and learning.
idiomatic: and that for emperors and kings, nothing is weightier than ritual and learning.

literal: Therefore in ancient state-building, teaching came first.
idiomatic: Therefore in founding a state, education came first.

literal: The state had the institutions of Bright Hall and Moat-enclosed Academy; the district had the ceremonies of village school and academy—all to draw forth what is hidden and stagnant, open and broaden talent and thought.
idiomatic: The state had the Bright Hall and Royal Academy; the villages had their schools and academies—all devised to draw forth hidden talent and broaden the mind.

literal: For in the fourth line of Hexagram Six there is the regret of an obstructed youth; the superior man greatly nourishes the work of rectitude.
idiomatic: For as the fourth line of Hexagram Six warns of a youth obstructed in learning, the superior man performs the great work of nurturing rectitude.

literal: Formerly Confucius was merely a grandee of the feudal states; he raised ritual and restored learning between the Zhu and Si rivers; talented youths from the four quarters flourished and turned toward his influence; more than seventy completed their studies and mastered the Way.
idiomatic: Confucius was only a feudal grandee, yet between the Zhu and Si rivers he revived ritual and learning. Talented youths from the four quarters flocked to him, and more than seventy completed their studies and mastered the Way.

literal: Since then, a thousand years of silence—surely the realm is not smaller than the state of Lu, nor are the wise and sage fewer than in former times; it is a matter of encouragement or its absence.
idiomatic: Since then a thousand years have passed in silence. Is the realm smaller than Lu? Are the wise fewer than in his day? The difference lies in whether a ruler encourages learning or neglects it.

literal: Recently we have suffered calamity without cause; the altars of state face the peril of a swaying tassel; bandit barbarians water their horses at the Yangtze; fierce rebels prowl a thousand li—so that the divine land lies desolate, turned to overgrown grass; within the four seas, human traces do not meet.
idiomatic: Recently we have suffered undeserved calamity; the altars of state tremble like a crown about to fall. Barbarian raiders water their horses at the Yangtze; fierce enemies prowl a thousand li. The heartland lies desolate, choked with weeds; within the four seas, men scarcely meet one another.

literal: Overlords have the worry of dining at dusk; the common people bear the pain of bitter poison; barbarian chiefs clash in the central plains—how can one hasten to matters of ritual vessels!
idiomatic: A ruler loses sleep over his meals; the people endure bitter suffering; barbarian chiefs collide at the heart of the realm—how can one speak of ritual vessels and sacrificial rites!
